elements.str: The concupiscences of the flesh may be compared to stables in which are donkeys, he-goats, and swine; and the affections of the spirit, to stables in which are thoroughbred horses, and also sheep and lambs.

etc. = interior truths in the Natural which are from the good there; for truths by themselves do not make the Natural; but good by truths. Hence its varieties are according to the quality of truth conjoined with good...
= truth from good. The reason these = what is of the interior Natural, is that these spices are purer than
= sensuous truth. The reason it = the affection of this truth, is its fragrance...
= the affection of sensuous truth, is that it is here mentioned first; for the incense was made up of four spices... and the one mentioned first is the most external.

= the affection of sensuous truth, cannot be confirmed from other places in the Word, because it is not mentioned anywhere else; but stacte of another kind, which is also expressed by a different Hebrew word, is mentioned among the spices which were carried down into Egypt (
The Lord... taketh away from Jerusalem the rod
If he rise again and walk abroad upon his staff
= the power which belongs to truth, thus forces; and
in like manner, but in reference to those who are not in good health; in which sense it is mentioned in,
remove the rod and the staff
) = the power and the forces of life from truth and good... In the Original Language,
is so called from leaning upon and being supported, which, in the Spiritual World, is effected through truth and good.
Like a hand when its staff is broken.
A man whose staff is in his hand for multitude of days
The bulls and cows (in Mercury) approach a species of stags and hinds. See
Free nations are like the great stags with lofty horns, which roam the plains, groves, and forests in full freedom.

Dippel appeared like a wild stag in bonds. Zinzendorf loosed his bonds, and set him at me, and he rushed furiously at me to lacerate and destroy me. (A dog then) rushed at the stag which was over me and evilly entreated it; and that huge stag was afterwards sent away into bonds elsewhere. The stag was Dippel...
He shall leap as a hart
) = he shall have joy from the perception of truth.
In the World of Spirits are seen stags, etc.
Of the Church when vastated it is predicated that
it shall stagger like a drunken man,
They stagger, but not with strong drink
At the presence of a little child they reeled... with anguish.
They shall reel to and fro
He who ascends from a lower Heaven... falters in his voice...
. ( = that they do not see the truths which belong to intelligence.
Like impure waters, stopped up, or stagnant.
The general delight in Hell is smelled as stagnant water...
From his hereditary stain, man is born into evils of every kind... and this stain is not removed unless the higher degrees are opened.
= such truth as is accommodated to what is scientific... The reason
= such truth, is that what is meant is the stem
= truths and goods; and thus the stem which is beneath them = a general vessel of truth; thus scientific truth. Explained.
That evils and falsities are dispersed as it were to nothing, is signified by
as the dust, and as the driven stubble
The house of Esau shall be for stubble
Every worker of wickedness shall be stubble
The first stamina may be called little vessels...
From the first thread of life...
This first form, as a stamen or initiament...
Why Moses, because he was a stammerer, calls himself
The tongue of the stammerers shall be swift to speak
) = that those who can with difficulty apprehend the truths of the Church will confess them from affection.
Abraham, he stood yet before Jehovah
) = the Lord's thought from the Human.
I stand by the fountain of waters
) = the state of conjunction of truth Divine in the Human.
) = to defend and take care lest falsities break in.
Behold he was standing by the river
When he stood before Pharaoh king of Egypt
) = the presence of the Celestial of the Spiritual there.
They who are in truth stand erect...
Not to be able to stand
) = not to be able to be present.
For this have I made thee stand
They stood at the door of the tent
) = ... that they were outside what is holy of the worship, etc.
In Heaven no one is allowed to stand at another's back...
= to hear and do what He commands. Illustrated.
They were seen as if lying down while they were deliberating; and as standing when they had come to a conclusion.
) = to be presented and gathered together to Judgment.
They stood round the table... and whispered devout praise to the Lord.
They stood, now, near the Angel; now, near the Satans, favouring those they stood near.
Certain appear standing in their places who told me they were walking.
= to be and to live; and
) = that they are subject to Him.
) = to be and to come forth from Him.
Which stand before the God of the earth
) = which are Divine things proceeding from the Lord, and are His in Heaven and the Church... To
= to be from Him; thus what is His in Heaven and the Church.
when said in the Word of Angels and the men of the Church, = to be from Him... for all the esse of Heaven and the world proceeds from the Lord... This proceeding Divine is called
which is called the Divine truth... and as this extends itself around the Lord in every direction, it is that which is properly said to
... for it looks to the Lord as its centre, and so therefore do the Angels who are recipients of it... from which it is that the Angels are said to
is properly said of the Divine truth, because it encompasses the Lord as a Sun.
= to be in the Divine truth, consequently with the Lord, in the following passages. Illustrated.
stand before the God of the earth
= the Divine which proceeds from the Lord, which is His in Heaven and the Church. That this, and those in it, are meant, may be evident from the fact, that to
stand before the God of the earth
is said of the two olive-trees, and of the two candlesticks, by which are signified good and truth, consequently the proceeding Divine.
= new life such as belongs to a regenerate man. Illustrated.
) = what belongs to the life of the intention from the will.
before Him = to regard and to understand what He wills.
I stood upon the sand of the sea
Lo a lamb standing upon mount Zion
Standing near the sea of glass
He said he was from the stars.
The very stars correspond: it is the Societies of Heaven and their habitations with which there is a correspondence of the stars; not that they are there; but that they are in such an order.

The Ancients (supposed) that the stars were the habitations of the Angels... And there is a correspondence; for in the other life there appears a heaven with stars; but... the stars there are the Knowledges of good and truth.
A little star (appears at man's resuscitation from the dead).
Wandering stars seen around a Spirit = Falsities; but not so when the stars are not wandering.
In his face were seen many wandering stars, which = Falsities.
The internal of such worship is described by...

elements.injection1: which are the Truths of faith

elements.str: They sometimes see a heaven... beautifully studded with little stars.
When the Lord pleases, good Spirits appear to others, and also to themselves, as bright stars, which sparkle according to the quality of their charity and faith.
When one contemplates the starry heaven, and thinks of the Lord's Kingdom.
) = a representation of goods and truths in a mental view of the constellations; (for)

wherever mentioned in the Word, = goods and truths; and, in the contrary sense, evils and falsities; or, what is the same, they = Angels, or Societies of them; or evil Spirits and their companies. When they = the former, they are fixed stars; but when the latter, they are wandering stars.

When the starry heaven appears (there), and the stars therein are fixed, it is known at once that they = goods and truths; and when the stars appear wandering, that they = evils and falsities. From the very glow and sparkling of the stars, it may be evident of what quality they are.
= goods and truths, or, what is the same, those in goods and truths, as the Angels. Illustrated.
) = goods and truths, or the Knowledges of good and truth, which at the consummation of the age... are thus darkened.
The Knowledges of good and truth, which are
will thus fall down and vanish. ( = the Knowledges of faith.
As the stars of the heavens
) = the multitude of the Knowledges of good and truth.
The spiritual are they who here and there in the Word are compared to

and this from the Knowledges of good and truth which they have; but not the celestial, because they have not Knowledges, but perceptions. Besides, the stars illumine the night, and the spiritual have a nocturnal light, as from the moon and stars, relatively to the light of day in which the celestial are.
or Knowledges, have relation to the Rational.
= the Knowledges of good and truth, which are of faith.
The stars have withdrawn their shining
) = the Knowledges of good and truth...
I will multiply thy seed as the stars of the heavens
It is chiefly the stars which are called
are signified truths; and, in the opposite, falsities.
Such suppose that the learned will there shine as the stars... But the learned, wise, and intelligent = those who are in good... and it is these who will shine as the stars.

I then saw a little star about the region of the left eye; and afterwards many little stars of a bright red colour, gleaming whitely... Lastly I saw as it were the starry heaven... These things represented the infundibulum in the brain, above which was the brain itself, which was signified by the starry heaven.
The stars shall fall from heaven
Those who relate to the interiors of the nostrils... have apertures opening at the side, through which they see as it were heaven with stars in a blue sky.
) = the Knowledges of good and truth.

= these Knowledges, is that they are small luminaries which shine at night, when they give forth into our atmosphere gleams of light, just as Knowledges give forth gleams of good and truth. Illustrated.
= the Knowledges of good and truth, they = also the doctrinals of the Church; for these are Knowledges.
= the Knowledges of good and truth. References.
Those (sensuous things) which are in the centre receive light through the Rational, and (appear there) as little stars which gleam and shed light around...
In those of (these infernals) in whom there is regard for what is good, this is sometimes represented by little stars, almost fiery, but not bright white.
A Spirit who appeared like a black cloud, around which were wandering stars. When wandering stars appear there, they = falsities; but fixed stars, truths.
Good makes every truth like a little star, in the midst of which there is a luminosity.
That then the Knowledges of good and truth perish, is signified by,
I will darken the stars of the heavens,
The Spirits of Mercury go forth outside the sphere of this world, into the starry heaven.
= the Knowledges of good and truth.
For the angelic abodes shine like stars; as is stated in
Those in that Heaven appear clothed in azure, spotted with little golden stars... When, in the world, they contemplate the starry leaven, they call it the abode of the Angels...
When there is any slight disagreement among (the Spirits of Jupiter), there appears to them as it were a thin bright white ray... or a little wreath
For by the starry leaven is signified the angelic Heaven.

The dwellings (in Jupiter) within, are spotted round about and above as with little stars, after the image of the heavens; for they want to exhibit within their houses a likeness of the visible heavens with their stars
; because they believe the abodes of the Angels to be there.
= the Knowledges of good and truth, which will no longer have light from faith and love, thus from Heaven, which is to
) = to be in the intelligence of truth and in the wisdom of good, and thence in eternal happiness; for
= the Knowledges of truth and good, from which are intelligence and wisdom.
The wise men... knew that a star would appear to them, concerning which Balaam... also prophesied (
= the Knowledges of internal good and truth which are from the Lord.
On the Earths in the starry heaven. General article.
cast some of the army and of the stars down to the earth
Their sun is one of the lesser stars.
I will multiply your seed as the stars of the heavens
are signified goods and truths as to Knowledges.

It was found that (the Spirits of the Fourth Earth) were from a star, which is their sun, very distant from the sun of our system; that its position is low down near the milky way; and that that star is among the lesser ones.
The sun (of the Fifth Earth) which to us is a star...
This human form appeared in a flaming beam, around which were little stars of the same colour. Thus did the Lord present Himself...
The sun (of the Sixth Earth) which to us is a star...
An angelic Society (was seen) as a cloud... with little stars round about... These little stars were Angels, who so appeared from light from the Lord.
= the Knowledges of good and truth, which are said to be
The star which went before them
Many have believed that they would shine as the stars...
) = the Lord as to the Knowledges of good and truth.
(which the dragon dragged down with his tail) = the Knowledges of truth.
The stellar forms in the brain.
The multitude of the glands of the brain may be compared to that of the stars; and the multitude of the fibrils from them, to that of the rays which go forth from the stars.
If wisdom is not conjoined with love, it is like a falling star.
In His right hand seven stars
) = all the Knowledges of good and truth in the Word, which are from it with Angels of Heaven and men of the Church.

When the Angels are below the Heavens, there appear around them as it were little stars in great abundance; and in like manner around those Spirits who, while they lived in the world, acquired the Knowledges of good and truth, or truths of life and of doctrine. These little stars appear fixed with those who are in genuine truths from the Word; but wandering with those who are in falsified truths... Hence it is evident that by
are signified the Knowledges of good and truth from the Word.
The mystery of the seven stars which thou sawest in My right hand
= the Church in the Heavens. ( = revelation of goods and truths, which are all from Him.
The seven stars are the Angels of the seven Churches
) = the New Church in the Heavens, which is the New Heaven. ( = those who receive goods and truths from the Lord.

There appears in the Spiritual World a heavenly expanse full of stars, as (here); it appears from the angelic Societies in Heaven; each Society there shines as a star to those below. From this they know in what situation the angelic Societies are.
These things saith He that holdeth the seven stars in His right hand
) = the Lord from whom are all truths, through the Word...
The seven stars in His right hand
= all the Knowledges of good and truth in the Word, which are thence from the Lord with the Angels of Heaven and the men of the Church.
I will give him the morning star
= the Knowledges of good and truth; and as through these there is intelligence and wisdom, these are signified by
The reason it is called the morning star, is that intelligence and wisdom will be given them by the Lord when He will come to instaurate the New Church. Explained.
These things saith He that hath... the seven stars
) = the Lord, from whom are... all the Knowledges of good and truth.
The stars of heaven fell unto the earth
In the Spiritual World, stars appear to fall from Heaven to the earth there, where the Knowledges of good and truth are perishing.
There fell from heaven a great star burning as it were a torch
The name of that star is called Wormwood...
A third part of the stars was smitten
) = that on account of evils from falsities and falsities from evils, they did not know... what any truth is...
= the Knowledges of truth and good from the Word. ( = that all the Knowledge of good and truth had perished.
By the light of the sun is signified Divine truth spiritual; and by the light of the moon and stars. Divine truth natural, both from the Word...
I saw a star fallen from heaven unto the earth
) = Divine truth spiritual inflowing from Heaven into the Church with them, exploring and manifesting.
here, = Divine truth spiritual, because it fell from the Spiritual Heaven. ( = Knowledges of truth which have been falsified, and thus turned into falsities.
in the plural, are signified the Knowledges of good and truth; and through these there is intelligence.
Upon her head a crown of twelve stars
His tail drew the third part of the stars of heaven, and cast them unto the earth

) = that through falsifications of the truths of the Word they have alienated from the Church all spiritual Knowledges of good and truth, and have utterly destroyed them through applications to falsities. ( = the falsification and adulteration of all the Truths of the Word.
That paper, when written on from the Word, shone like a star.
As the Angels withdrew... stars appeared around their heads.
from the light with which He came into the world; on which account He is called
from the light which will arise from Him before the New Church... For by
is signified the light from Him, which in its essence is wisdom and intelligence...
The prince's robe was set with stars of a silver colour wrought in needlework.
The paper on which the arcana were written, ... while it was in the Spiritual World, shone like a star...
The infinity of God the Creator may be seen from the infinite number of the stars, which are so many suns, and thence so many worlds.
(The notion that) the stars are only luminaries which originated from our sun.

(I said to the Angels), In the world there appear innumerable stars, greater and less, which are so many suns, and which merely transmit light into the world of our sun; and when I saw that in your world also stars are to be seen, I supposed that these are as many as those in the world. The Angels were delighted with this discourse, and said that perhaps there are as many, because every Society of Heaven sometimes shines like a star to those who are below; and the Societies of Heaven are innumerable, all ordinated according to the varieties of the affections of the love of good... and, as these were foreseen before the creation, I suppose that there have been provided (an equal number of stars in the natural world).
The apostolic Church was actually like a new star appearing in the starry
The Word, in the shrines of the temples there, shines like a great star, and sometimes like the sun.
When the Angels descend from Heaven to perform any duty below, they appear encompassed with little stars, especially around the head; which is a sign that Divine truths from the Word are in them.
I saw fatuous lights, some like sheets of paper full of writing, which... at last appeared like falling stars, which in their descent vanished in the air. Explained.

Faith in the Lord, when destitute of Truths, may be compared to a new star appearing in the expanse of Heaven, which in time grows dim; but faith in the Lord, together with Truths, may be compared to a fixed star which remains constant... The faith of Truths shines in Heaven like a star.
That the Lord is the Son of the living God, is like the morning star to all who enter His Church.
Round the Angel's head appeared a lucid band, in which were minute stars.

They viewed predestination as a star descending from heaven... not knowing that a falling star is a meteor of fatuous light, which, when it falls into the brain, can confirm every falsity... until it is believed to be the true light, and is decreed to be a fixed star; and finally is sworn to be the star of stars
Whether they believe that the stars of heaven will fall upon the earth, which is smaller than a single one of them.
The fall of Spirits from Heaven as stars.
On the seats of some in Heaven who are called stars.
On those who are called stars of the dragon.
That a star in the zenith fell down with the rest.
The appearance of little stars is a good sign.
Evil spirits also have stars around them.
Their face appears beset with many wandering stars... These wandering stars = an appearance of what is honourable in externals.
Around (this evil Spirit) were small wandering stars in abundance.
On the appearances to Spirits of little fires, and stars.
They who are in Truths of faith, that is, who are led by the Lord, appear like bright little stars in the hemisphere.
That there is no fixed star which has not its Earths around it.
On inhabitants of the starry heaven.
There appeared an azure starry heaven...
Evil Spirits seen around me as innumerable Wandering stars.
They look upwards to the stars, and have a revelation thence.
The ordinances of the moon and stars, from which is the light by night
) = truths from spiritual good, and from Knowledges, from which there is intelligence.
That he-goat then appears to tread the stars under his feet. (Just as in
The stars from their courses fought against Sisera
) = the Knowledges of truth, and combat from them against the falsities of evil.
) = the Knowledges of truth from good.

The stars cannot fall to the earth, because they are larger than the earth; consequently by them are signified such things as are of heavenly light, and give light, which are the Knowledges of good and truth. Moreover, stars appear in the angelic Heaven; but they are appearances from the Knowledges of good and truth; and therefore they appear around those who are in such Knowledges, especially when they are turning them over in their minds, and when they long to know them.
) = in the heights where those dwell who are in the Knowledges of truth.

As the Lord is the east, a star was seen by those from the east; and, as they were in Knowledge about the advent of the Lord from the representatives among them, the star was seen and went before them, first to Jerusalem, by which was represented the Church as to doctrine and as to the Word, and thence to the place where the infant Lord was. Moreover,
= the Knowledges of good and truth; and, in the supreme sense. Knowledge about the Lord.
is predicated of the stars - by which are meant the Knowledges of good and truth from the Word
= the Knowledges of truth and good.
That the Lord has infinite power, may be evident from the fact that... He has created the universe, full of such innumerable stars, which are suns...
Profaners of this kind appear at first with a face of a human colour around which float many wandering stars...
Those (Africans) who had believed that God had been born a man, saw a bright star in the air.
The six states of man's regeneration. Signified, Defined.
The third state of the Most Ancient Church.

All these states are so preserved... that not the least of them is lost. (For) every state of a man, from infancy to old age, not only remains in the other life, but also returns, and that exactly as they had been while he lived in the world; thus not only the goods and truths of the memory, but also all the states of innocence and charity; and, when the states of evil and falsity recur... these states are tempered by the Lord by means of the [good states].
But with the good all their good states... return.
The four states after temptation. Treated of.
Changes of place there are changes of state.
Places and distances there are nothing but varieties of state.
The four states of the first Ancient Church. Treated of.
When the state is changed, the end also is changed; and, with the end, the thought.
The beginning of the ninth state, which was the last. Signified.
The Angels are not in the idea of place and time, but in that of states.

They never change their places except as their state is changed; and, as the state is changed, the places and distances with them are also varied. But as everyone has a general state... and the particular and individual changes of state relate to the general, after these changes they come back to their own situation.
(Thus) the walking about and translations, and the progressions, of Spirits... are nothing but changes of state.
The Lord advanced from an obscure state to one more lucid. (The five states of this advance. Enumerated, Signified.)
The Lord's first state, when He was born. Treated of.
Progression into a lucid state. Signified, Explained.

There are neither quarters nor times (there), but states... The states of intellectual things are as the states of the times of the day and year, and also as those of the quarters. The states of the day are those of evening, night, morning, and noon; the states of the year are those of autumn, winter, spring, and summer; and the states of the quarters are those of the sun, in its relation to the west, north, east, and south. Similar to these are the states of intellectual things... In Heaven, those are in light who are in a state of wisdom and intelligence, exactly according to their state; and those are in the greatest light who are in a state of the highest wisdom and intelligence.

Therefore, whenever travelling, sojourning, and passing from place to place, occur in the Word, nothing else is suggested to the Angels than such change of state as they have. There are changes of state of both the thoughts and the affections. Changes of state of the thoughts are Knowledges, which (there) are produced by instructions.
There are two states from which there is heavenly light. Explained.
By external worship... man is gifted with states of holiness... which are preserved to him by the Lord for the use of eternal life; for all the states of his life return (there).
The first state of His external man. Signified.
The Lord appears to everyone according to his state, as in this case.
The things which inflow are received according to the state of each person.
According to the state of the Spirits around me, and thus according to my state.
The ideas are varied... according to the changes of the state.
A state of union then. Signified.
The Lord's two states, of glorification and humiliation.
The relativity of the Lord's state. Signified, Explained.
The state of perception in which the Lord then was. Signified.
(Man ought to) rise up thereinto a continually more perfect heavenly state.
The six states (of the Spiritual Church which is in the good of charity, but in external worship) as described in the history of Lot, Enumerated.
The four states of those who are against charity in that Spiritual Church. Enumerated.
After temptation, there remain from it many states of truth and good, to which their thoughts can afterwards be bent...
These (organic) forms are varied and changed according to the changes of the state of the affections and persuasions.

They afterwards perceive that space and time are not there, but state instead; and that (there) states correspond to spaces and times in nature; to spaces, states as to being; and to times, states as to manifestation
A full state of unition. Signified, Explained.
Man's state is then said to be full. Explained.
The Lord's first state, when He thought of that Rational being separated from Himself: that it was a state of grief from love. Signified.
A change of state towards that Rational. Signified.
The first state of those being reformed and becoming spiritual... is that they think they do good and think truth from themselves...
The second state of those being reformed, is that they are reduced to ignorance... even to despair. Treated of.
The state of thought of those who are in desolation of truth, and in consequent despair. Signified.
(What inflows from the Lord) manifests itself only by a change of state of the man's affection.
That the Lord thoroughly knew its state. Signified.
This is effected by the state of anxiety and grief even to despair. What is good, blessed, and happy, no one can perceive with exquisite sense, unless he has been in (a contrary) state.

(Although convinced by reasons) their state of thought about their own prudence is not changed by it, except at the moment... and, after the lapse of a few moments, they return to their former state of opinion... for unless the affection is subdued, the thought remains in its own state... But when anxiety and grief are induced upon them... even to despair, their persuasion is broken, and their state is changed. (Another example.)
(This is why) those being reformed... are reduced into (this) state of vastation, and, when they are in this state even to despair, they then for the first time have comfort and help from the Lord.

The first state after desolation, which was a state of consolation and of the hope of help, was described in the preceding verse; and their second state after desolation, which is a state of enlightenment and consequent refreshment, is described in this verse. As these states are unknown in the world... we may describe the state of those being regenerated in the other life...
This state, which is one of instruction, treated of in this verse, is the third state of those coming out of desolation...
A place and state of temptation. Signified, Explained.
The Lord's state at that time according to perception. Signified, Explained.

The state the Lord took on... when He underwent the most grievous and the inmost temptations. Treated of. His first preparation for this state was that He entered into a state of peace and innocence...
Many states exist together, and these distinct from one another.
The Lord from His Divine could induce upon Himself whatever states He pleased; and He prepared Himself for temptations by inducing many states.

(These) puttings on by the Lord of various states must be unknown to man, because he never reflects upon his changes of state, which are nevertheless going on continually... All his states are from (the action of the Spirits and Angels with him), and thus are directed by the Lord to eternal ends.

In every state there are a great many others, which do not appear, and which together appear as one general state; and these states are disposed in relation to the states which follow in order in their series. With man, these things are done by the Lord; bu with the Lord... they were done by Himself.

The changes of state... with man, and the order in which they follow, and the series through which they pass, and thus how they are bent by the Lord as far as possible to good (are most minutely perceived by the Angels).
The Lord alone knows the times and states.
The times and states of the Church as to the truths Divine which had preceded. Signified, Explained.
The first state (of the new Spiritual Church). Signified, Explained.
Their second state, in which they indeed give assent, but still wish it to be from themselves; (and) their third state, which is a state of belief that they are reformed by the Lord. Signified.
Their fourth state follows, in which they perceive it to be from the Lord.
Adapted to their state. Signified, Explained.
All being regenerated are gifted with charity and faith... but each according to his capacity and state. Explained.
(For) the Lord alone sees man's state; not only his present, but also his future one to eternity.

For man, when first born, is introduced into a state of innocence, that it may be a plane for all the rest of the states, and be the inmost in them... Next, he is introduced into a state of the affection of celestial good... afterwards into a state of the affection of spiritual good... As he advances in age, he is introduced into a state of the affection of truth... The last state is a state of wisdom, in which is the innocence of infancy; and thus the first state and the last are united.
These states did not exist once only; but continually during the Lord's whole life.
The new state is the state of glorification of the Rational... in respect to truth.
The change of state (effected by regeneration) cannot be seen in the man's body, but in his spirit.
A state representative of the Lord as to the Divine itself. Signified, Explained.
The Angels have no idea of the ages of man... but instead they have the idea of states. Enumerated.
As the Lord completely changed His human state into the Divine one, so, when He regenerates man, He completely changes his state.
The first state of the man who is being regenerated. Described.
= a change in the state of the Church.
That motion means a change of state. Explained.

In themselves, the space and time (there) are changes of state; for this is their origin... By changes of state induced in others, Spirits cause them to appear in another place... Man himself, in so far as he is in a state of affections and thence of joy; and in a state of thoughts, and thence of absence from the body, is not in time... because his spirit has states to which the spaces and times in the external man correspond. Motion, therefore, being successive progression in space and time, is, in the internal sense, change of state.

The Angels, who are not in the idea of time, but in that of state, perceive most clearly (what the Divine was before time); for the eternal with them is not the eternal of time, but the eternal of state.
The Angels derive nothing from time, and space; but from state as to being and as to manifestation.
= the entire state here treated of.
For of interior things is predicated state, which is signified by place; but of exterior things, doctrine.
A state of temptation as to the natural good of truth. Signified, Explained.

(External things cannot be brought into) obedience to the internal man, except... by many new states into which the man is introduced, which are states of acknowledgement of [the quality of] self, and of acknowledgement of the Lord... thus states of humiliation...
The first state of the perversion of the Church, Signified, Explained.
The second state of the perversion of the Church. Signified, Explained.
When the state was at hand. Signified, Explained.
The state of the regeneration of man; here, the quality of his first state... for this state is entirely inverted relatively to that in which man is when he has been regenerated. Treated of.
Still less (can man perceive) the changes of state (of the good and truth of the Natural).
If man's ends are for good... he is in a state of regeneration; but if the ends are for evil... he is in no state of regeneration.
Progression and change of state. Signified, Explained.
A great alteration about the inversion of state. Signified, Explained.
(For) in the state before regeneration, truths apparently dominate; whereas in the state after regeneration, good receives the dominion. References.
In man's fourth age... the state is full. Explained.
The Angels have changes of state between the highest degree of light, and a less degree... and these changes of state are as the morning... the midday... the evening... and then the morning again.
When the Angels are in a fuller state of reception, they are in their peace and happiness; otherwise they are in a state of unrest and of some anxiety.
For in the other life everyone may easily be let into a state of life which he had had here, because the state of his life remains with everyone after death.
It has treated of three states of the perversion of good and truth in the Church; and here it treats of the fourth state, which is also the last. (These four states enumerated.)
(In judging his ends) a man should attend to the various states in which he is; for the states themselves very much vary the perception.
A new state of life. Signified, Explained.

All times = states; thus years, months, and days; but the quality of the states is evident from the numbers affixed. But when a year, month, or day is mentioned in the singular, it = an entire state; thus the end of a preceding, and the beginning of a subsequent state.
All states, also, have their periods; that is, their beginning, successive progress, and end; yet in the other life these are not perceived as times; but as states and their evolutions.
A full and holy state. Signified, Explained.
All affections... are variations of that celestial and spiritual light... and hence come the changes of state.
The first state of the Church is described by
For when man is being regenerated... he is led through many states. The general states are what are designated by the twelve sons, and afterwards by the twelve tribes.
As the Angels are not in space and time, they have ideas of state.
There are two states, a state which corresponds to space, and a state which corresponds to time. The (former) state is state as to being; and the (latter) state is state as to manifestation...
(The superiority of the state after death.)
But with the Lord there are no states; for all with Him is eternal and infinite.
The first state of innocence. Signified, Explained.
(These things) are varied according to all the states of life; and the states of life are varied in general according to the ages; and in particular according to the affections.
In interior things... nothing is perceived by spaces and times... but by states and their variations and changes...
He was in a state of tranquillity, as of a kind of peaceful sleep. Explained.
In order that man may be brought from the state of the old man into the state of the new...
As the states of his life are to be so greatly changed...
This may be illustrated by the changes of state (in man's successive ages).
Thus the former things are always left behind when a new state of life is put on.
But when man is being regenerated, his state becomes altogether different... nor does anyone arrive at this state except by the means of regeneration...
The change of state with that (middle) good (
His changes of state are nothing but changes of Societies.
How the case is with the middle goods by which man is brought from the state of the old man to the state of the new man.

Representations are according to changes of state as to good and truth; and changes of state are according to the changes of the Spirits and Angels. Explained... Man's state is altogether according to the Societies of Spirits and Angels in the midst of whom he is... But his changes of state are quite different when he adjoins the Societies to himself... from what they are when the Societies are adjoined to him by the Lord. Explained... From the Societies, the Angels perceive the states which are with a man... while man has only an obscure perception of what Societies are with him through some changes of state from that source.
(Four states of separation from the good signified by
A state of use and of end of good. Signified, Explained.
The middle kind of Spirits are sent back into the state of their good, and therefore into a state of use and of end therefrom...
A change of the state signified by

The states of Spirits as to good and truth are according to the Societies in which they are... Thus when they are removed from one Society into another, the states of their thoughts and affections are changed, and consequently their state as to truth and good.
For changes of state (there) are in general nothing else than approaches to the Divine, and removals from it.
A change of the state signified by
For the end of a state of conjunction is the beginning of a following state, which is one of separation.
In a man being regenerated (the Angels) see and perceive in this way all the changes of his state; and, according to them... they lead him to good...
A state of love in which the good signified by
A state of good in somewhat of that conjunction. Signified, Explained.
The state if the separation were of its free will. Signified, Explained.

Man does not know... how the state of every good is changed... With those being regenerated, there are changes of state of goods, from infancy to (death)... But how it is with the changes of state of the goods, the man knows nothing... because he has no Knowledges...
The inversion of state in the Natural. Treated of.(in
The quality of the Lord's state (then). Signified, Explained.
But... the Divine states which the Lord had when He made the Human in Himself Divine, do not fall into any human apprehension, except... by the states of man's regeneration.
To space and time in the Heavens correspond states and changes of states.
States of conjunction through temptations. Signified. For the man then enters into a spiritual or celestial state.
The state at that time as to goods and truths - that it would not appear to anyone. Signified, Explained.
The state which precedes is always as an egg to the one which follows.
The state of the life of good from truth at that time. Signified, Explained.
Their perceptive faculty is varied according to the general changes of state of the Society in which they are.
It is the state (there) which makes the appearance.
Aristotle was then let into the state of his life he had (here)...
For man after death carries with him all the states of his life. Example(s).
What state they were in. Signified, Explained.
The changes of state of the affections appear to the life in the faces of the Angels. Described.
The states of good Spirits and Angels are continually changing and perfecting...
The state of the things which follow. Signified, Explained.
There are, in general, two states, a state of god, and a state of truth. The state of good is called a state of being, and the state of truth, a state of manifestation.
A change of state as to truths. Signified, Explained.

As state, and change of state, are so often mentioned... they shall be explained. Time, and the succession of time, or space, and the extension of space, cannot be predicated of the interior things of man... because they are not in time or place... but are in interior things which correspond to these; and these interior things we have to call states, because there is no other word to express them. The state of the interiors is said to be changed, when the mind... is changed as to the affections and derivative thoughts; as from sadness to joy... These changes are called changes of state; and they are predicated of the affections, and of the thoughts in so far as they are ruled by the affections; but the changes of state of the thoughts are in those of the affections as singulars are in generals, and are, relatively, variations.

The thought of Spirits and Angels is from states of life, without any notion of times; (because) the progressions of their life are not distinguished into different ages... They are in the interior memory... and the thought from this memory has not times and spaces adjoined to it; but states and their progressions instead. Thus they correspond; and (therefore) times, in the Word, = states.
In the Spiritual World there is a continual progression of states from one into another; and consequently in the last of every state there is a first or beginning, thus a continuation...
When one state is terminated and another succeeds, which is a noteworthy one, it is indicated by
and a change of state less noteworthy, by
That that good was prior in time, not in state. Signified, Explained.
After some unfoldings of the state of his life, it became manifest that he was deceitful.
All the times of the day and year = various states according to the variations of the light of Heaven.
The states of the re-birth of each Sensuous, and of each thing in the Natural and Rational, have their progressions from beginning to end... and then they commence from a certain new beginning...

The periods of the first state are from truths to goods... After (regeneration) charity... becomes the beginning, and from it new states commence, which proceed in both directions - towards what is more interior, and also towards what is more exterior. Explained.

In the interior Heaven there is no idea of interior and exterior... but there is the idea of more perfect or more imperfect state; for interior things are in a more perfect state than exterior ones...

The last of the state. Signified, Explained... By the last of a state is meant when a prior state comes to an end, and a new one begins. A new state begins in a man who is being regenerated, when the order is changed...

With every man, whether being regenerated or not, there come forth changes of state, and also inversions; but in one way with those being regenerated, and in another with those not being regenerated. With (the latter) these changes or inversions are from (natural) causes. Explained. But with (the former) the changes or inversions are from spiritual causes... and when the man begins to be affected with what is good, he is in the end of the prior state, and in the beginning of a new one.
In that new state. Signified, Explained.
(Perception) concerning the state of disjunction. Signified, Explained.
When the state is full, that is, when all things in the Natural are prepared to receive the influx from the interior...
The state of temptation relatively to the state after it, is like the state of a pit or prison. Described. This state, when presented to view in the other life

elements.injection1: where all spiritual states can be exhibited to the sight

elements.str: The states of the multiplication of truth in the interior Natural. Signified, Explained. (And in the exterior Natural.
The last state of desolation. Treated of.
This is the first state, and is called the state of reformation. Explained. Most in the Church are introduced into this state... yet few are regenerated...
The first states when truths are multiplied into series. Signified, Explained.
The series themselves... are varied according to the changes of state.
The subsequent states of desolation. Signified, Explained.
A new state is here described.
The end of this state. Signified, Explained.
Every such General... has its receptacle, within which it can... vary its forms, and change its states.
Motions in the other life, and progressions, are nothing else... than changes of the state of life. Explained.
In that World there are neither spaces nor times; but states of life instead. In externals, these states produce a vivid appearance of progressions and motions.
Truths according to the state of each. Signified, Explained.
The change of state of each among themselves. Signified, Explained.
= an unexpected and sudden change of the state of the thoughts.
When the state (in regeneration) is changed, and becomes inverted, there is mourning; for they are then let into temptation... Representation.
That the associates... should return to their former state. Signified, Explained.

Love is the Harmonic resulting from changes of state and variations in the forms or substances of the mind... Thus love is the Divine which inflows into the forms, and disposes them, so that the changes of state, and the variations, may be in the harmony of Heaven.
The Spirits are changed according to the man's states, that is, those of his affection...
The commotion which then comes forth, manifests itself by anxiety arising from a change of the former state...

How the case is with the state of life of Spirits and Angels... This state in Heaven is that Spirits and Angels have their morning, midday, and evening, and also twilight, and morning again. Explained.
No one state is exactly like another to eternity; nor does one Spirit or Angel pass through changes of state like those of another...
The varying states in the other life are according to the perception of good and truth, thus according to the perception of the Lord's presence...
The state and quality of the spiritual life which had been in the Natural from the Spiritual. Signified.
All numbers in the Word = the state and quality of the Thing treated of.
The full term of this state. Signified.
Desolation after the full term of this state. Signified.
By desolations and temptations, states contrary to heavenly life are perceived, and there is induced a sense of the happiness of the heavenly life...
The entire state of the Thing represented by Jacob, and its quality. Signified, Explained.
The state just before regeneration. Signified.
The separation (of Spirits bound to me was affected by) changes of state of the affections.
The greater the extension is, and the more it is according to heavenly order, the more perfect is the state.
I have frequently perceived these elevations (into a more interior light), and at the same time the changes of state as to the affections and as to the thoughts.
These variations (of the form of the mind) come forth according to the changes of state of the affections.
The states of intelligence and wisdom (in Heaven) are varied according to the lights. Example(s).

For all the states which a man has acquired (here), are retained (there), and are infilled. With the good, the good states are retained and infilled with good, and through these states these are elevated into Heaven; and with the evil the evil states are retained and infilled with evil, and through these states they fall down into Hell.
What would befall everyone when in such a state. Signified, Explained.
By the sons of Israel, or the tribes named after them, are described all the states of the Church as to goods and truths; thus as to the spiritual life of everyone within the Church.
A full state. Signified and E.
The first state, where there is the good of truth. Signified, Explained.

The reason distance is perceived (there), is from the state of the affection of truth and good: in proportion as the state of one Society differes from the state of another, the Societies appear far apart.

As to the changes of the state of man's life, it is inconstant, and is carried upwards and downwards, that is, towards Heaven and towards Hell. But they who suffer themselves to be regenerated, are continually being carried upwards, thus into more interior heavenly Societies. Explained.
An Angel spoke with them by means of changes of state.
= the end of a former state and the beginning of a new one.
The state of the Church, such as it is now, is described in what follows; also the state of its external.

The Church with man undergoes new states by turns; for as a man is strengthened in the truth of faith and good of charity, he is introduced into other states; and the former state serves as a plane for the following state, and so on continually.
This is the first state with the man who is being regenerated. Described.

These are the two states (of regeneration) which are meant by the origin of truth from good, and their conjunction. But the truth conjoined with good, here signified, is not such as is received by man in the first state. Explained.
It is the second state which is here described. The first state was a state of immission among evils and falsities. This second one is a state of the insinuation of the good of the Church.
It is the third state which is described in this verse.

Here begins the fifth state of the progression of the law Divine in the Lord's Human; in the relative sense, of the progression of the law Divine with the man who is being regenerated; which is one of separation from falsities, and of adjunction with the truths of simple good.
After many changes of state. Signified.

Those Angels and Spirits who are similar as to states of life, appear to be near each other; and thus Know each other; whereas those who are unlike as to states of life, appear to be far from each other, and thus do not Know each other. In a word, in the other life, likeness of state causes them to appear present and to be Known; and unlikeness of state causes them to appear absent and not to be Known.

There is no other access to the Divine, because it is above the things of place and time, and is in those things with man which are called states; namely, states of love, and states of faith; thus states of each faculty of the mind... By these, man can approach the Divine. Treated of.

In Heaven, instead of space and time, there are states... But in the Divine which is above the Heavens, there is... not even state; but instead of space there is infinity, and instead of time, eternity.
Every change of state contains infinite things, and also every least part of it.
For evils and falsities cannot be removed, and goods and truths be insinuated in their place, except by many changes of state.
So long as they are in this state (of infestation) they are as it were in hard service.
When Spirits have the state of evening and night, their thought is in a forced state... But when they have the state of morning and midday, their thought is in a free state...
They so appear (on the two opposite sides of Venus) according to the states of their life; for the state of life presents all the appearance of place and space.
The state and quality of the law from the Divine... as it was among those of the Spiritual Church at the first time of visitation. Signified, Explained.
The state and quality of doctrine. Signified.
Hence (the spiritual sight) can admit influx from Heaven according to the states of the Things.
Influx according to the state (of falsity in which the infesters were). Signified, Explained.
For everything has its own state, in which, and according to which, it is.
Hence all Divine miracles represent states of the Lord's Kingdom.

It is according to order that states of affection and thought cause the idea of place and distance (there); and that they appear to be distant from each other in proportion as they are in a diverse state... Magicians abuse this law... by inducing on others changes of state, and thus translate them now on high, and now into the deep; and they also cast them into Societies in order that they may serve them as Subjects.
The end of that state after truths were falsified. Signified.
The diversity of state causes (the Spirits of the different Earths) to appear separate from each other, either to the right or to the left, at a greater or less distance.
In the ideas of the Angels there is nothing from time and space, but instead of them there are states. Explained.

But the light from the spiritual Sun is Divine truth, and the heat is Divine good; and from these there come forth with the Angels ideas of states; states of intelligence and of faith, from Divine truth; and states of wisdom and love, from Divine good. The variations of these states with the Angels are the things to which correspond the states of light and shade (here), and also those of heat and cold.
That there may be an end of that state as to the falsities of malevolence. Signified, Explained.

Every miracle done in Egypt = a peculiar state into which come those in the other life who are in falsities, and infest. There are ten states into which they come in succession, before they are completely stripped of all truth, thus before they are cast into Hell.
Besides, in the other life man enters new states, and undergoes changes. Explained.

A full state. Signified. By a full state is meant an entire state from beginning to end: for every state has its beginning, its increasings, and its maximum; and this full term is what is meant by a full state; and is signified by
That this state is the principal one of all the states. Signified, Explained.
The beginning from which are all the sequent states to eternity. Signified, Explained.
A state of initiation of the interiors. Signified, Explained.

A full state. Signified, Explained... It is called a full state when the good is such that there is nothing wanting for receiving the influx of innocence. Explained... But the state is not full when truths have not yet qualified good, so as to make it capable of receiving a corresponding state of innocence. This state becomes full for the first time when truths are regarded from good; and it is not as yet full when good is regarded from truths. In the latter state are those being regenerated; in the former one are those who have been regenerated.

These two states (of regeneration) are accurately distinguished in the Word; for the reason that man cannot be in both states at once. He who is in the first state cannot enter into the second until he has been regenerated; and he who is in the second state must not betake himself to the previous one; (for he then) relapses into the state of faith... and also beyond it. Signified.
The duration of this state before a state of illustration in Heaven. Signified, Explained.

These two states are entirely different, as are the state of the means to an end, and the state of the end. When the state of the end has come, the things contained in the state of the means will have been passed through.
A state of means to the end through temptations. Signified, Explained.
Because there was then a state of charity and faith, through which there was separation from those in evils and falsities. Signified.
In the beginning of a holy state. Signified, Explained.

This fermentation or combat, comes forth especially when the state with man is turned... For the state has not been purified while the man acts from the truth of faith; but it has been purified when he acts from the good of charity; for he then acts from the will.
The first state, of truth from good, in which there is nothing of what is false. Signified, Explained.

The second state is described in a subsequent verse... These are the two states in which those of the Spiritual Church, when in good, are kept by the Lord: the first, that from the good which is of the will they see and think truth; the second, that from this marriage of good and truth, they produce truths, which, by willing and doing them, again become goods; and so on continually.
The first state of departure, and its quality. Signified. For the journeyings of the sons of Israel = states of life and their changes from the first to the last.
The quality and state (of the infestations). Signified, Explained.
When they have a full state of remains, they are elevated into Heaven. Explained.
What is meant by a full state... Everyone has a certain measure... which is filled in the other life... This state is what is meant by a full state, and is signified by
In the beginning of a new state. Signified.
The second state after they were delivered. Signified.

For the journeyings and encampments of the sons of Israel, after they had gone forth from Egypt = the spiritual states of those who have been delivered by the Lord. The changes of states are signified by the journeys from one place to another, and their stay there.

By these things was represented the state of Heaven; for there are perpetual variations and changes of state there; because the Angels are continually being perfected, which cannot be done without perpetual changes of states. Explained.
A change of state into evil with those in falsities from evil. Signified, Explained.
It is the states of truth and good; and, in the opposite, of falsity and evil, which are represented (there) by heights and depths. Explained.
A state of good from the Divine. Signified, Explained.
A state of illustration and affection, thus of consolation after temptation. Signified, Explained.
What is successive of life as to states of temptations. Signified. For those of the Spiritual Church... are led from one temptation into another.
At the end of each state. Signified, Explained.
This disposition (of goods) is effected by the Lord at the end of each state, which is signified by
That at the end of the prior state there is a revelation that they are delivered. Signified, Explained.

In the Spiritual World there are perpetual changes of state; and all there pass through them. The reason is that they may be constantly perfected; for without changes of states... they would not be perfected. The changes of states which succeed each other in order like the times of the day and of the year, never return exactly the same... The beginning of every state corresponds to morning on earth... and the end of every state, to evening...
That in the beginning of a new state there is the coming of the Lord. Signified, Explained.
That at the end of the state good will be appropriated through delight. Signified, Explained.
For a state of morning (there) is when spiritual good is in clearness... and a state of evening is when natural good is in clearness...
That in the beginning of a new state they will have as much good as they can receive. Signified, Explained.
A state of reception and of application to use. Signified, Explained.
The end of the state. Signified.
The beginning of a new state. Signified.
= a state of peace, when there is no temptation.

These two states (of regeneration) are the inverse of each other; for in the former state truth dominates; and in the latter, good; or, in the former state, the man looks downwards or backwards; and in the latter, upwards or forwards. When a man is in the latter state... he is no longer allowed to look back, and to do good from truth... Signified.

= states of combat and labour; here, a state of the reception of truth, that is, a state when good is acquired through truth; for in this state there are labour and combat. In this state, man is let into temptations... But after this state, there is a state of the conjunction of good and truth, thus a state of rest even for the Lord. It is this state which was represented by the rest on the seventh day... This state is the one meant by the second state, mentioned in
This state is the state of Heaven...
That up to the end of the former state. He gives, through truth, so much of good that conjunction may afterwards be effected, Signified, Explained.
A state of peace, in which the conjunction of good and truth is effected by the Lord; for all conjunction of these is effected in that state. Signified.
That we are to remain in this state. Signified.

The prior state (of regeneration) is signified by the six days which precede the seventh; and the latter state, by the seventh day. (Thus) the prior state was represented by the journeyings of the sons of Israel in the wilderness for forty years; and the latter state by their introduction into the Land of Canaan.

The Divine Providence... continually leads to salvation, and this by various states; now glad, now sorrowful; which states man cannot possibly comprehend; yet all are profitable to his life to eternity.
When the state of combat with the falsity from interior evil ceased. Signified, Explained.

For this is the second state (of the man of the Spiritual Church), which comes forth after he has undergone temptations. For while he acts from truth, he is tempted... but when the truths with him have been confirmed, they are reduced into order by the Lord, and (then) he enters the second state, which is, that he wills truths and does them...
The separation (of good which is from the Divine) hitherto relatively to the state of those of the Spiritual Church. Signified, Explained.

For in their first state, good does not appear, but only truth... In the first state, the action is from truth, not from good; but in the second, from good. In the first state, good is as it were absent... But in the second state, when good is acted from, good is present.
The conjunction (of good) in the state before regeneration while there are temptations. Signified, Explained.

When man is in the prior state, namely, when he acts from truth... he is in a state of undergoing temptations. Through these, he is successively brought to the second state, namely, that he acts from good, that is, from charity and its affection. When, therefore, he comes near this state, he is said to
encamp at the mount of God,
that is, at the good from which he afterwards acts.
A mutual Divine celestial state. Signified, Explained.
The disposition by truth Divine with those of the Spiritual Church in the state before [the action is] from good. Signified, Explained.
In both states (of regeneration) man is led by the Lord, but in the first one through immediate influx; and in the second one, through influx both immediate and mediate. Representation.
The first state (of regeneration) is described in these words.
In every state, interior and exterior. Signified, Explained.
It treats here of the first state

elements.injection1: that in which man is before regeneration

elements.str: In such a state are they who are led by the Lord through good. Described.
That those of the Spiritual Church shall be led to a state of good. Signified, Explained.

In the preceding verses it treated of the prior state of those of the Spiritual Church when being regenerated, namely, when they are led by the Lord through truth. To this state succeeds another, which is that they are led by the Lord through good. This change of the one state into the other is what is described in this chapter by [the doings of]. Jethro.
The fulness of the state. Signified, Explained.

Every state has its beginning, its progression, and its end. When a state arrives at its end, it is full, and is called the fulness. In the other life, all things are measured by the progressions of state, and their successive changes from the beginning to the end... Hence, in Heaven, instead of times there are states. Yet as in the inmost sphere of Heaven there is a certain progression according to the Divine heavenly form... and as, according thereto the states of all in Heaven undergo changes, the Angels are alternately in the good of love, the truth of faith, and obscurity as to both. It is from this that there is a correspondence of the states there with the times (here). Enumerated.

There are in general two states of life, namely, a state of thought... and a state of affection... The state of thought relates to the truth of faith; and it is this state which is enlightened by the light from the Sun of Heaven... whereas the state of affection relates to the good of charity; and the heat of the will... in man is from the heat of that Sun. Hence it may be evident how the case is with states and their changes in the other life; and what is meant by the fulness of the state which is signified by
The state here, of which fulness is predicated, means the prior state which those of the Spiritual Church had undergone... And now the second state is described.
They came to the wilderness of Sinai
= a state of good in which the truths of faith are to be implanted. Explained.
What is continuous of life from the prior state. Signified, Explained.
How the case is with the two states with the man being regenerated. Explained, References.

With those of the Spiritual Church there are two states, a prior one when, through truths, they are led to good; a posterior one when they are in good, and, from it, in truths; here, when they are in good in which truths are to be implanted, which state is a middle state between the prior and the posterior one. Treated of.
A state when in good. Signified, Explained.
A Divine state in which there is revelation. Signified, Explained.
A Divine state relatively to those who will receive. Signified, Explained.
The heavenly state which is around. Signified, Explained.
The consequent state of life in Heaven. Signified, Explained.

The prior state is when the man is led by means of the truths of faith to the good of charity; the posterior state is when he is in the good of charity and thence in the truths of faith. Through the prior state, man is introduced into the Church, in order to become a Church; and when he has become a Church, he is in the posterior state. The goods and truths with him in the posterior state are signified by
but the truths and goods with him in the prior state, by
The garments of Angels and Spirits are varied according to the changes of the state of faith or truth in which they are...
The first state with truths. Signified, Explained.
The beginning of the following state, when the life is from good. Signified, Explained.
The state of life then from good. Signified, Explained.
The good which man does in the first state (of regeneration) is called the good of faith; but the good he does in the second state... is called the good of charity...

For the spaces and times (there) are states; and hence distances are diversities of states. But still, before the external sight there, states appear as spaces, and their diversities as distances. References.
Six years thou shalt sow the land
= the first state when the man of the Church is being instructed in the truths and goods of faith.
In the seventh thou shalt let it rest
= the second state, when the man of the Church is in good, and thus in the tranquillity of peace.
In the Word, especially the prophetic one, the one state and the other are distinctly described.
); and that from it no one is to return to the first state. References.
That these states are distinct, is involved (in

), for by these commands is signified that he who is in a state of truth cannot be in a state of good, that is, in the second state; nor conversely. The reason is that the one state is the inverse of the other; for in the first state the man looks from the world into Heaven; whereas in the second state he looks from Heaven into the world; for in the first state truths enter from the world through the Intellectual into the will, and there become goods, because of love; whereas in the second state the goods thus produced go forth from Heaven through the will into the Intellectual, and appear there in the form of faith.
A state of labour and combat when in external delights which are to be conjoined with internal ones. Signified, Explained.
A state of good when in internal ones. Signified, Explained.
The state of life of those who are in truths and goods outside the Church. Signified, Explained.
From the beginning of a new state. Signified.
The second state of deliverance from damnation, which was a state of the implantation of truth in good. Signified. (by the second feast.)
That the good of innocence of the posterior state is not to be conjoined with the truth of innocence of the prior state. Signified, Explained.
Even to a full state. Signified.
Therefore they who are in a state of Hell cannot be transferred into a state of Heaven. Signified.
= the opposition and contrariety of the states of life.

The things in the Word which are of life in a spiritual and in a natural state. Signified, Explained... It is said in a spiritual state and in a natural state, because with every man there are in general two states; one, which is peculiar and proper to the internal man, which is called the spiritual state; and the other, which is peculiar and proper to the external man, which is called the natural state. Explained.
The successive states of the Church in this Earth as to the reception of truth Divine... are meant by the statue seen by Nebuchadnezzar. Enumerated.
in a place = to remain in one's state.

= while in a state of truth... For there are two states (of regeneration); the first is called a state of truth; and the second, a state of good. Explained... When man is in the state of truth, he is outside Heaven; but when he is in good, he is in Heaven, thus is introduced to the Lord. Moreover, when man is in the first state, he is in labour and combat; for he then undergoes temptations. But when he is in the second state, he is in rest and the tranquillity of peace. The former state is that which is represented in the Word by the six days which precede the seventh; and the latter state by the seventh day. References.

The spirit is not led through spaces, but through variations of the state of the interior life... and approaches are effected according to the agreements or likenesses of the states; for agreement or likeness of state conjoins, and disagreement or unlikeness disjoins.
A similar state of the Thing for all the truths. Signified, Explained.
All states of the good of love and truth of faith are signified by
the four corners of the earth;
states of the good of love, by the corners of the east and west; and states of the truth of faith, by those of the south and north.
There are four states to which correspond the four quarters in the world. Enumerated.
(Perpetual influx from the Lord) constantly in every state. Signified, Explained.
In every state of good and of truth in worship. Signified, Explained.
For all things which belong to motion, as walking, etc. = a state of life. References.
Such a state of the Divine good in the Spiritual Kingdom. Signified, Explained.
= to induce the state of the thing which is represented by the garments.
= the following state, which is of Divine truth proceeding from the Lord's Divine good in the Heavens.

(Thus) there are two states with a man who is being regenerated; the first, when the truths of faith are being implanted and conjoined with the good of charity; the second, when he speaks from the good of charity through the truths of faith, and acts according to them; thus the first state is from the world through the natural man into the spiritual, thus into Heaven; and the second is from Heaven through the spiritual man into the natural, thus into the world... This circle is the circle of the regeneration of man...

(So) the first state of the Lord's glorification was to make His Human Divine truth, and to unite it with the Divine good which was in Him; and the second state was to act from Divine good through Divine truth... By the sacrifice from the bullock, and the burnt-offering from the first ram, the first state is described; and by the infillings of the hand from the second ram, the second state; and, lastly, by the sacrifice from the bullock, and the burnt-offerings, is signified its continuity.
The first state (of glorification, or of regeneration) is described by,
In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and God was the Word;
all things were made by Him, and without Him was not anything made that was made.
The spiritual and celestial goods which had not been conjoined to the new state. Signified, Explained.

A new state is every state of the conjunction of good and truth, which is when a man who is being regenerated acts from good... There is a new state also when those in Heaven are in the good of love... There is a new state also when an old Church ceases, and a new one begins. All these new states are signified by
The good of innocence in every state. Signified, Explained.
The removal of evils through the good of innocence in a state of love and the derivative light in the internal man. Signified, Explained.
For in the Heavens the states vary as to love and the derivative faith, as in the world the times vary...

The man who is being regenerated, and also the man who has been regenerated, also undergoes variations of state as to love and as to faith, through elevations towards interior things, and depressions towards exterior ones; but few are capable of reflecting upon it...
etc... as are also the states of the Church...

The Church in general is circumstanced as is man in particular; his first state is a state of innocence... his second is a state of light... his third state is when he begins to love the world and self... and his fourth and last state is when he does not care for truths, and still more when he denies them. Such states are also the states of every Church from its beginning to its end; its first state is a state of infancy, thus of innocence, and consequently of love to the Lord... its second state is a state of light; its third state is a state of light in obscurity... and its fourth state is a state of no love and thence of no light, which is its
The like in a state of light and love in the external man. Signified, Explained.

With the Angels, there is a continual succession of such states; and they are continually being perfected through them. These variations come forth... from the state of the interiors of the Angels themselves; for, like men, they desire to be in their internals at one time, and in their externals at another. Explained... This is the origin of the variations of the states of the Angels. The reason they have such states, and such variations, is that the Sun of Heaven is the Divine love itself; and therefore the heat which proceeds from it is the good of love, and the light is the truth of faith.

That he who is in good, which state is the state of the regenerate man, must not return into a state of truth, which was his prior state when being regenerated, for in this state man is led by means of truth to good, thus partly by himself; whereas in the posterior state... man is led by good, that is, by the Lord by means of good. Signified.
When the state of love is in clearness. Signified, Explained.
A state of intelligence of truth and good. Signified, Explained.

From his first infancy to extreme old age, man undergoes many states as to his interiors, which are states of intelligence and wisdom. The first state is from birth to the fifth year: this state is a state of ignorance, and of innocence therein, and is called infancy. The second state is from the fifth to the twentieth year: this state is a state of instruction and knowledge, and is called childhood. The third state is from the twentieth to the sixtieth year, which state is a state of intelligence, and is called adolescence, young manhood, and manhood. The fourth and last state is from the sixtieth year and upwards, which state is a state of wisdom, and of innocence therein. Illustrated.
While the first state lasts, the interiors are being formed. Explained.
The second state is not as yet a state of intelligence. Explained.
But the third state is called a state of intelligence. Explained.

And the last state is a state of wisdom, and of innocence in wisdom; and exists when the man no longer cares to understand truths and goods, but to will and live them; for this is to be wise. Explained.
From the succession of these states, the man who is wise can see the marvellous things of the Divine Providence, which are that a prior state is continually a plane for those which follow...
The states of Spirits and Angels vary as to love and faith, just as the times of the days and years vary as to heat and light...
Their garments vary according to the changes of their state as to truths.
In Heaven they do not think of time, but only of changes of state as to the affections and derivative thoughts...
A holy state then from the appropriation of Divine truth purified from evil and the falsities of evil. Signified, Explained.
The state of the external when the internal from the Lord inflowed, and it received information. Signified, Explained.

With men there are two states as to the things of the Church, worship, and the Word: some turn themselves to the Lord... some to themselves... (The former) receive influx and are in illustration, and thus in the perception of truth inwardly... But the latter can receive no influx... and are in thick darkness concerning all things of the Church, worship, and the Word. Signified.
Six days shall work be done
= the first state of the regeneration of man... (and of) the glorification of the Lord's Human.

For man has two states while being regenerated: a prior one when he is in truths, and through truths is led to good; and a posterior one when he is in good, and from good sees and loves truths. In the prior state, man is indeed led by the Lord, but through his own proprium; for to act from truths is to act from the things which are with man: but to act from good is to act from the Lord. Further explained.
In the seventh day there shall be holiness to you, the sabbath of a sabbath to Jehovah
= the second state of the regeneration of man, when he has conjunction with the Lord; and, in the supreme sense, the union of the Lord's Human with the Divine Itself. Explained.

I was brought to another Earth... by changes of the state of my mind...
